newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index dips, heavyweights mostly flat.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index dips, heavyweights mostly flat.

text.p: Profit-taking on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) continued to push down the BUX index on Wednesday but at a slower pace, traders and an analyst said.

"Probably what is happening now is a necessary correction to just bring valuations back to some kind of reasonable level," said James Oates, director for central and eastern Europe of UBS in London. "The last few weeks have been very strong."
The BUX index finished at 6,256.68 points, down 36.23 points or 0.58 percent. Spot share turnover fell to 2.41 billion forints from 3.99 billion on Tuesday.
Traders said a selling wave began on Tuesday and the BUX fell 70.02 points following seven successive daily record highs.
At the end of Tuesday's session, the prices already found strong support and began to recover, but on Wednesday morning the selling pressure returned, traders said.

"Probably the investors appeared who decided too late on Tuesday to sell, " said Andrea Keresztesi, trader of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. "But at the end (of the session) the buying side rebounded... and the index went upwards."
Most heavyweight shares, which on Tuesday joined the falling trend, moved sideways on Wednesday with the exception of pharmaceuticals Egis and OTP Bank.
"Both have risen too rapidly recently," Keresztesi said.
Egis closed at 11,630 forints, down 120 forints or one percent, while OTP fell two percent or 90 forints to 4,410.
Keresztesi said Hungarian share prices were likely to stabilise around current levels this week and to rise for the longer term.
Oates said investors were waiting to see corporate earnings reports for the first half of the year.
"The rise that we have seen obviously reflect the hopes of the economy, but it has got to the stage where the valuations of Hungary now are very expensive."

"I think that the prices will correct until we see more solid earnings growth coming through," Oates said, adding that Hungarian companies showed much improvement in earnings recently, but investors wanted to get a clear picture of first half earnings.
